title: Military Calisthenics. Air Force PT Test Prep.
author: Matt B.
desc:
Repeat Weekly. Designed to be ran alongside regular workout programs, or as a stand alone program to prep for an upcoming test.

With the Air Force's massive update to the Physical Fitness Assessment (PFA) governing the transition to a 2-mile run and the rebalanced 100-point scale (Cardio 50 pts, Waist-to-Height Ratio 20 pts, Strength 15 pts, Core 15 pts), training needs to evolve.
​To score a 90+ "Excellent," we cannot just practice doing casual push-ups; we need to build muscular power, specialized endurance, and specific pacing for the longer run.

Also, under the updated guidelines, your Waist-to-Height Ratio (WHtR) is a massive 20% of your total score. The calculation is simple: Waist Circumference (inches) ÷ Height (inches). Keeping this ratio below 0.49 locks in a perfect 20 points before you even step on the track. Keep nutrition clean, focusing on whole, dense protein sources and high-volume fiber to ensure structural body composition remains in the "Low Risk" point bracket.

ex.note: 5-7 mins. Perform arm circles, shoulder rolls, and light jumping jacks to lubricate the shoulder joints and prime the nervous system.
Classic Push-Ups: Chest to the floor, full lockout at the top. Hold top of final rep for as long as possible.
Find something to lock your feet under. Always keep hands planted on chest, touch elbows to knees/quads. Rest at the top or rep if needed.
Wide-grip. Full-lockout on bottom. Chin above bar at top of rep. Dead hang as long as possible after final rep.
2-Mile run. ​Progression: Increase your total weekly speed (reduce time) by no more than 10% per week to protect your joints and tendons.
Static stretches. Flex the target muscle and "push" in the opposite direction as you "pull" into the stretch. Hold for 45 seconds - 1 minute per muscle.
Arm circles, band pull-aparts, and 2 light sets of 10 standard push-ups to prime the shoulders.
Elevate your hands on blocks/parallettes to increase the range of motion, or perform diamond push-ups. Focus on a controlled 3-second descent and an explosive push.
Vertical pulling prevents shoulder injuries from high-volume pushing and strengthens the upper back.
Practice the 2-minute alternative style. Lower completely to the deck, lift your hands briefly, and explode up. This forces strict mechanics and chest recruitment.
10-minute dynamic jog, including high-knees, butt-kicks, and 3x 50-meter strides.
Run 400 meters (1 lap around a standard track) at a pace significantly faster than your target 2-mile test pace. Rest 90 seconds. Repeat 6-8 rounds.
5-minute easy walk and dynamic lower-body stretching.
1 minute push up trail. Perform 1 full minute of maximum effort, clean-form push-ups. Do not break form until the buzzer sounds. Track your count. Rest 3 minutes between sets.

1 Minutr sit up trail. Perform 1 full minute of maximum sit-ups, keeping your fingers interlocked behind your head or across your chest according to local testing guidance. Rest 2 minutes between sets
This alternative core test component trains the hip flexors and lower abdominals intensely, protecting the lower back while ensuring you maximize your core points.
Burnout volume for the triceps and anterior deltoids to lengthen endurance capacity during the final 15 seconds of your official push-up test.
5-minute light walking and dynamic mobility movements.
Target-Paced 2-3 Mile Threshold Run. First mile: Easy base pace. Remaining miles: Settle precisely into your Target PFA Goal Pace. (e.g., if aiming for a 14:00 2-mile, lock in a 7:00/mile pace)
5-minute walk and deliberate static hamstring, calf, and hip-flexor stretching.
